diagnosis.incident_summary: Inventory has been overselling since 09:12 UTC because the 06:00 WMS stock file transferred as only 60% complete while reporting SUCCESS; no rule caught it for over three hours, and the incident was only raised manually by warehouse ops at 10:15.

timeline.description: stock_position_0600.csv transferred, status SUCCESS, 4.1MB (usual ~6.8MB) — trailer declares 128,400 rows but only 77,032 actually arrived
ELK-R-MFT-004 file transfer monitor: stock_position_0600.csv status=SUCCESS — the rule checks the status flag only, never declared_rows vs actual_rows, so it passes cleanly
reservation confirmed for SKU MRD-30217 qty 6 — exceeds available stock position (stale WMS data)
oversell rate climbing: 14 orders affected in last 30 min, all against stock positions sourced from stock_position_0600.csv
INC0098480: Multiple oversells traced to WMS stock file — manual escalation

hypotheses.cause: The 06:00 WMS stock file (stock_position_0600.csv) was silently truncated at the source — only 77,032 of 128,400 declared rows actually arrived, so inventory-reservation has been working from a stale, incomplete stock picture since 06:00

supports.why: The transfer trailer itself declares 128,400 rows but only 77,032 arrived, and the file size (4.1MB vs a normal ~6.8MB) is consistent with roughly 60% of the data — this is a real, checkable mismatch in the transfer record, not an inference.
The first oversell lands exactly three hours after the truncated transfer, against a SKU whose stock position could only be wrong if the source file were incomplete.
Every oversold order traces back to stock positions sourced from this same file — a single common root, not scattered SKUs, which argues against a general demand effect.

contradicts.why: The MFT job reported SUCCESS and the dedicated file-transfer monitor rule also passed at 06:05 — both signals said the transfer was fine, which is precisely why nobody looked at the file for over three hours.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: If the export job logs showed a clean, complete write for the 06:00 run, that would rule out truncation and reopen the investigation toward a genuine demand or reservation-logic issue.

hypotheses.cause: A genuine demand spike is causing legitimate oversell against otherwise-correct stock data

supports.why: A rising oversell count over successive 30-minute windows is superficially consistent with organic demand outpacing correct inventory.

contradicts.why: The description explicitly ties the oversell to stale WMS data sourced from the 06:00 file, and every affected SKU traces to that same transfer — a volume-driven oversell would be expected to spread more evenly rather than concentrate on one file's data.

hypotheses.what_would_change_this: If oversells were spread across SKUs with no relationship to the 06:00 transfer, or if a later, complete stock file failed to resolve them, that would support a genuine demand-driven read instead.

ruled_out.reason: Different service (nightly-settlement-batch), no shared correlation ID, unrelated to inventory or MFT.
Same unrelated nightly-settlement-batch job; timing is coincidental.

checks.action: Compare declared_rows to actual_rows in the 06:00 transfer trailer
checks.if_result_b: Row counts match — rules out truncation, reopens the investigation

checks.action: Cross-reference oversold SKUs against the row range missing from the truncated file
checks.if_result_a: Oversold SKUs fall within the missing row range — confirms hypothesis 1 precisely
checks.if_result_b: No overlap — points away from the truncation as the specific mechanism

checks.action: Check OMS-EXPORT-01's job log and exit code for the 06:00 export run
checks.if_result_a: Non-zero exit / kill signal partway through — confirms the export was killed mid-write
checks.if_result_b: Clean exit code — the truncation happened somewhere in transit instead of at the source

downstream_degraded: fulfilment-dispatch (will need cancellations/backorders for oversold SKUs)

recovery.proposal: Trigger an out-of-band re-export and re-transfer of the current WMS stock position, force-refresh inventory-reservation's cache from the new file, and freeze reservations on the affected SKU range until the refresh completes; separately notify fulfilment to flag the 14+ oversold orders for manual backorder or substitution.
recovery.risk: Freezing reservations on affected SKUs will itself cause some checkout failures for a short window; if the out-of-band export also fails partially, the stale-data problem could reoccur.
recovery.rollback: If the re-export introduces new inconsistencies, revert inventory-reservation's cache to the previous (stale but internally consistent) snapshot and keep the SKU freeze in place until a verified file lands.

diagnosis.post_incident_note: INC0098480 — root cause: 06:00 WMS stock file transfer truncated at ~60% (77,032 of 128,400 rows) while reporting SUCCESS; the file-transfer monitor rule (ELK-R-MFT-004) checks status only, not row counts, so nothing fired for over three hours until warehouse ops manually escalated. Mitigated via out-of-band re-export and cache refresh once approved. Follow-up: add a declared_rows-vs-actual_rows check to ELK-R-MFT-004 (or a dedicated rule) so a SUCCESS status with a row-count mismatch alerts immediately instead of passing silently.

diff.changed_summary: The OMS export job log confirms the mechanism directly: the source export process was killed by a host memory-pressure eviction at row 51,368 of 128,400, which is why the transfer reported SUCCESS (the file that existed at kill time uploaded cleanly) despite being incomplete — this closes the last open question against hypothesis 1.

what_changed: Exit code 137 (SIGKILL) at row 51,368 confirms the export was killed mid-write by a host-level memory-pressure eviction on OMS-EXPORT-01, not a network truncation in transit or an MFT-side bug — this points the fix at OMS-EXPORT-01's resource limits, not the file-transfer layer.
The demand-spike alternative had no plausible mechanism left once the SIGKILL evidence landed; it stays ranked 2 for completeness but is now considered closed.
